Validation

Source: vignettes/articles/validation.Rmd
validation.Rmd

rendehR is validated by a harness that is kept in the development repository and run before every release. It does not use package code to check package code: raw counts come from the PhysioNet files read as untyped text, and concept selection, parsing, unit conversion, ICD normalisation and cohort derivation are re-implemented from their specifications. The last level compares rendehR with ricu on the same admissions. This page summarises the run for version 1.0.0.

Two profiles

Profile Data Cohorts
Demo the open MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV and eICU-CRD demo datasets all patients, spinal cord injury (SCI), Sepsis-3, a random identifier list
Full the complete MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV and eICU-CRD releases the SCI cohort

The demo profile runs every level, including the package’s own test suite and R CMD check; the full profile repeats the data levels at scale.

Levels

Level What is checked
L0 Environment, raw-file checksums, no credentials in outputs
L1 R CMD check, the test suite with every database test enabled, test safety, documentation, configuration linters, every vignette re-knitted on the demo data
L2 Parsing, units, ICD normalisation and credentials on synthetic inputs
L3 Each pipeline stage’s pre- and post-conditions on real data
L4 Row conservation, concept selection, unit conversion and event-level tracing back to the raw files
L5 Demographics, mortality and value plausibility
L6 Identical rebuilds with other threads and chunk sizes; resumed imports
L7 Bad inputs fail loudly; destructive operations are guarded
L10 The explorer’s numbers against independent SQL, its statistics, and every page and tab opened in a browser
L11 Cohort, static variables, time series and exposures against ricu 0.6.3

A check passes, warns or fails. A warning is a documented property of the data (for example ICU stays recorded outside their admission in the source); known differences from ricu are listed with their expected shape in a register, and count as explained only when that shape is measured.

Full data: the SCI cohort

  • Cohort. 46,513 admissions (MIMIC-III 4,320, MIMIC-IV 39,850, eICU-CRD 2,343). Admissions, patients and ICU stays match ricu exactly in every source.
  • Build. The three sources take 73 minutes from raw files to the merged schema, with a peak memory of 71 GB.
  • Determinism. A second build with other thread counts and import chunk sizes gives identical content in all 975 tables.
  • Static variables. Age, sex, hospital mortality and length of stay agree with ricu for 100% of the shared admissions; height and admission weight, where rendehR pools more sources by design, for 85-100%.
  • Time series. 63-64 concepts per source reproduce ricu row for row (admission, minute, value); 9-12 of them per source differ by a documented definition, and the difference has the documented shape.

Distance between the value distributions of rendehR and ricu (Kolmogorov-Smirnov D over all values of each concept, 0 = identical):

Source Concepts Mean D Largest D
MIMIC-III 54 0.0010 0.038 (SpO2)
MIMIC-IV 58 0.0013 0.023 (direct bilirubin)
eICU-CRD 54 0.0006 0.014 (magnesium)
All 166 0.0010 0.038

163 of the 166 concepts have D at most 0.01, and none exceeds 0.05.

Check totals for 1.0.0

Profile Checks Pass Warn Fail Error
Demo (4 cohorts, every level) 1,129 1,097 18 1 0
Full (SCI cohort) 314 301 11 0 0

The rows do not add up to the checks: the demo totals also hold 12 checks of earlier known failures that now pass and 1 registered known failure, the full totals one check that now passes and one skipped check (a destructive check that the demo profile covers). The one demo failure is known and minor: concept values are stored with three decimals, which a synthetic check of full precision flags.

Highlights of the demo run: R CMD check with 0 errors and 0 warnings; the test suite with 4,235 passing tests offline and 4,756 with every database test enabled, which leave every existing table of the test database intact; all 11 vignettes re-knitted from scratch; and all 31 pages and tabs of the explorer opened in a browser without an error.

How a run is recorded

The harness needs a PostgreSQL server, the raw PhysioNet files and ricu 0.6.3. Each run records every check with its level, status and evidence, and the totals; comparing two runs lists the checks whose status changed. A written plan describes every check and its pass criterion.
